findings.statement: Higher baseline CXCL8 is associated with ustekinumab non-response (BH padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000102]), but it also separates UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0154]), so it marks severity rather than a drug-specific mechanism. Golimumab, infliximab and vedolizumab arms are not significant.

CXCR2, the top convergence candidate, is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]) but equally in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126]); the drug-vs-placebo interaction is null (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.982]). It is a severity marker, not a ustekinumab-specific one.

CXCR2 ranks first in convergence (expression, replication in eight cohorts, genetics, literature, tractability), with meta-analysis log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814]; clinical-stage antagonists of CXCR1 and CXCR2 exist (reparixin, navarixin, ladarixin, SX-682). Expression is largely neutrophil-linked, so a composition effect is likely.

OSM is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]); the UNIFI placebo arm does not reach significance (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]), but the interaction is not significant and golimumab shows nothing (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.994]). Evidence for a drug-specific OSM effect is therefore weak.

TREM1 is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]) and also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]), consistent with severity.

Baseline IL23A, the ustekinumab target pathway, is not associated with ustekinumab response (padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]); no arm survives correction. Response labels carry inflammatory-severity signal, not target-expression signal.

NFkB pathway activity is higher in non-responders to ustekinumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]) and in UNIFI placebo (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]), so it is non-specific severity; the PROTECT mesalazine arm shows no difference (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.5-ASA (PROTECT).padj=0.414]), while the PROTECT corticosteroid arm does (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.corticosteroids (PROTECT).padj=0.00174]).

TNFa pathway activity is higher in infliximab (GSE16879) non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.000294]) but this does not replicate in ACT1 infliximab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab (ACT1).padj=0.23]); it is also raised in other arms and UNIFI placebo, so not anti-TNF-specific.

JAK-STAT activity is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]) but not in vedolizumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.571]), a weaker and more arm-restricted signal than NFkB.

TGFb pathway activity is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000493]) but not in golimumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.348]); UNIFI placebo is also significant, so it tracks severity.

In the adalimumab single-cell atlas CXCL8 shows no baseline difference between remission and non-remission; after treatment it falls in cycling mononuclear phagocytes (padj [gene=CXCL8; type=antitnf_singlecell; source=DATASET:GSE282122; after_vs_before_treatment.1.padj=0.0253]) and rises in enterocyte/TA states. Small cohort: a lead only.

CHRDL2 is the top first-in-class candidate (up in eight cohorts, antibody-tractable) but only a fraction of its signal is retained after composition adjustment ([gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.2764]); it comes mainly from inflammatory fibroblasts. Highest vital-organ RNA is [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6], the highest of the lead candidates, a safety flag.

LAX1 (T/NK lineage, antibody-tractable) is up in eight cohorts with low vital-organ expression ([gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=2.5]), but composition retention is low ([gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.23]), so the increase largely reflects lymphocyte infiltration; no response data link it to a drug.

XKR9 is the only top-15 discovery candidate classed as intrinsic (epithelial; retained [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.7976]), but it is up in only [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=4] cohorts, and single-cell expression is sparse (plasma cells are the top inflamed cluster share). Replication is the missing element.

caveats: Treatment cohorts are small outside UNIFI (e.g. golimumab, infliximab, vedolizumab non-significant arms are underpowered, not evidence of absence).
Associations only; non-responder status in UNIFI is dominated by severity, and placebo arms share the signal.
Discovery candidates are mostly partly composition-driven and lack functional validation, genetics and response data; novelty reflects few UC papers, not proven benefit.
Not all top-15 discovery genes and convergence candidates (CXCL1, DUOX2, IDO1, MMP1, AQP9, CD274, CHI3L1) were profiled for response; CHI3L1 treatment record was retrieved but not written up.
